headline: Advance Permit Planning for Angels Landing and Canyon Access
reservation: Entry requires a standard park pass, but specific high-demand activities require separate seasonal lotteries. The Angels Landing hike requires a permit for the chained section, and wilderness permits are necessary for overnight stays or top-down Narrows trips. Systems change frequently; verify current lottery windows and shuttle requirements on the official NPS website before travel.

days.title: Canyon Floor and River Corridors

stops.name: Riverside Walk
stops.detail: Follow this paved path to the Temple of Sinawava to see the canyon walls narrow toward the Virgin River.

stops.name: Court of the Patriarchs
stops.detail: A brief walk leads to a viewpoint for the three towering sandstone peaks.

days.driving: Allow 30-60 minutes for shuttle transfers; conditions vary.
days.note: During shuttle season, private vehicles are restricted in the main canyon; use the Springdale and Park shuttle systems.

days.title: High Desert Elevations
days.start: Suggested: 7:30 AM from Zion Canyon Visitor Center

stops.name: Angels Landing
stops.detail: If you hold a required permit, ascend this strenuous ridge for panoramic views of the canyon floor.

stops.name: Scout Lookout
stops.detail: A turnaround point for those without permits, offering a steep climb and broad vistas.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes for shuttle and staging; conditions vary.
days.note: Check the official flash flood potential rating daily, as rain upstream impacts canyon safety.

days.title: East Side and Slickrock Views

stops.name: Zion-Mount Carmel Tunnel
stops.detail: Drive this historic engineering feat to access the park's eastern high country.

stops.name: Canyon Overlook Trail
stops.detail: A moderate walk providing an expansive view of the Pine Creek Canyon and the lower switchbacks.

days.driving: Allow 1-2 hours for mountain road transit and tunnel queuing; conditions vary.
days.note: Parking near the tunnel is extremely limited; have an alternative plan if spots are full.

intel.title: Shuttle Requirements
intel.text: The Zion Canyon Scenic Drive is primarily accessed via shuttle for much of the year. Check the official seasonal schedule as private vehicle access is prohibited during operation hours.

intel.title: Springdale Staging
intel.text: Parking at the Visitor Center often fills early in the morning. Utilize the Springdale town shuttle to reach the pedestrian entrance if park lots are at capacity.

intel.title: Gateway Supplies
intel.text: Refuel in Springdale or La Verkin before entering the park's interior. No fuel is available within the Zion Canyon Scenic Drive or on the East side toward Mount Carmel.

intel.title: Connectivity Limits
intel.text: Cellular service is unreliable within the deep canyons and near the tunnel. Download official maps and permit confirmations for offline use before leaving Springdale.

intel.title: Midday Heat
intel.text: Exposed trails like the Watchman can reach high temperatures by noon. Plan strenuous uphill segments for early morning and use the shuttle for shaded sightseeing later.

plan.arrival: Collect your vehicle at St. George Regional Airport (SGU), then stop in St. George for major supplies before the 70-minute drive to Springdale. Check-in logic depends on shuttle timing, so aim to drop bags early.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are suitable for paved roads, but RVs face strict size restrictions and escort fees at the Zion-Mount Carmel Tunnel. Check rental agreements for off-pavement restrictions.
plan.goldenHour: Canyon Overlook for sunset, though actual lighting on the sandstone varies by season.
